item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds only the requested convenience API and reuses multipartbody.NewFile without unrelated API or retry-layer changes. It still should delegate to FilesService.Add and needs stronger tests before merge.","reasons":["B preserves FilesOption behavior and avoids adding the association fields explicitly forbidden by the contract.","B uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", the supplied filename, and a buffered bytes.Reader body suitable for retries.","A introduces multiple forbidden association options, NewFileWithFields, and extensive unrelated changes to RawClient request-body ownership and generic retry behavior.","A duplicates option validation, request construction, response decoding, and error handling inside Upload instead of routing through Add; B makes the same delegation mistake but with far less machinery and churn to correct."],"risks_a":["Directly violates the instruction not to add association fields or refactor unrelated request/retry machinery.","Changes caller-body closing semantics and replay behavior across Raw.Do, Files.Update, picture uploads, and other consumers, greatly expanding compatibility risk.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than FilesService.Add, duplicating the lower-level path the contract requires to remain authoritative."],"risks_b":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than FilesService.Add, violating an explicit architectural requirement.","The multipart test checks the field and filename but never reads and verifies the uploaded content.","Retry coverage uses a bytes.Reader directly at the transport layer and does not verify that streamed Upload content is encoded and resent identically after a 429; validation and source-reader failure tests are also missing."]}
